paragraphs.source_en: I wanted the colors to be consistent and to convey information. Someone suggested that we use a modified *National Geographic* scheme: shades of red would represent shallow water, shades of blue deeper water. We also came up with standard schemes for water assignments. *Santa Fe*’s water would always be blue in military exercises (American forces are always “blue”); other submarines would be yellow; areas where we shared water but were separated by depth zone would be—you guessed it—green! A quick look at the chart and each OOD would know instantly that if it was blue, *Santa Fe* owned the water; if it was yellow, we needed to stay out; and if it was green, we needed to maintain a specific depth zone. This worked because the display conventions in efficient symbology and coloring tapped a much larger body of knowledge in your brain. It built on what you already knew.
